newsitem.title: UK: Bourses break records, Swiss franc suffers.
newsitem.headline: Bourses break records, Swiss franc suffers.

text.p: The Swiss franc, hit by jitters in the country's banking sector, fell to a 21-month low against the dollar on Tuesday while European bourses followed New York's soaring Dow higher with London and frankfurt hitting new peaks.

The Swiss franc's tumbled to 1.2921 to the dollar and to a 20-month low against the mark of 84.84 centimes. It came after share index heavyweight Union Bank of Switzerland's shares fell over two percent when it announced heavy costs for a restructuring.
But analysts said UBS was just a symptom and the market was worried about the Swiss banking sector as a whole and the country's general economic outlook.
"Bad loans in the banking sector are being caused by the continued weakness in the economy. Many Swiss banks are in the same boat with problems over bad debts," said a trader at a Swiss bank.

Elsewhere on the currency markets the dollar firmed somewhat to around 1.5275 marks and against the yen it was retaining a firm foothold well above 112.00 ahead of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) fourth-quarter Tankan survey of business sentiment due at 2350 GMT.
Analysts said the BOJ's survey would be a crucial gauge of what the Japanese economy is doing and interest rate prospects

"If we get a strong Tankan, the yen will do well on the back of that, and we could see dollar/yen retracing back to 111.00 yen. But if it comes in line with expectations then, I don't see it having a major impact," said Yamaichi's Chester.

The dollar also gained ground against the French franc as the lorry drivers' strike intensified and as Bank of France Council Member Paul Marchelli was quoted as saying French interest rates should be cut as soon as possible.

With the exception of Paris -- hit by the truckers' protest -- Leading European shares were boosted by the Dow's overnight 1.71 percent surge -- its biggest one-day points gain since August. On Tuesday, Wall Street opened hesitantly then continued its climb and was soon up 15 points.

Britain's blue chip FTSE 100 index opened sharply higher ahead of Tuesday's budget, setting an intra-day record at 4,094.4, up 28.3 points, before slipping slightly. The previous FTSE record was 4,073.2, set on October 21.
Traders said hopes for a "prudent" non-inflationary budget from Chancellor Kenneth Clarke (starting at 1530 GMT), coupled with New York's performance, had been the motive force.
"We are bound to start getting a bit nervous after the initial reaction to Wall Street," said one dealer. "I expect us to drift back and stocks to turn mixed until we see what Clarke has to say."

Traders said they expected to see the corporate sector's tax burden increase to offset any drop in personal taxes designed to woo the electorate ahead of a general election which must be held by May next year.

In Frankfurt, German shares ended bourse trade at another record close, but slightly off the day's high, boosted not only from Wall Street but also from the firmer dollar, which makes German exports more attractive.
The 30-share DAX closed floor trade up 11.45 points at 2,810.64, off the day's high of 2,819.95 points.
In Paris, French shares retreated into negative territory on concerns about the franc and fears the truckers strike could provoke widening labour unrest.
Eurotunnel continued to suffer and was down 6.43 percent at 6.55 francs after last week's fire in the Channel Tunnel.
CURRENCIES AT 1515 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.65 yen and 1.5275 marks against 112.62 yen and 1.5208 marks late on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1515 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 23.8 points higher at 4,078.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 2.37 points at 2,274.77.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 11.45 at 2,810.64.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $374.50 compared with Monday's close of $375.05. Silver was off four cents at $4.77. Platinum was fixed at $379.00 an ounce, the lowest fixing since December 10, 1993.
